QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_72

question.text: Under SAS-1300 the chief LIMITATION of E-Diksha-style financial-literacy programmes is that:

answer.text: Behavioural change is hard to sustain — knowledge gain at training may not translate into long-term behaviour; the SIA must measure 6-12 month post-training behaviour as the outcome, not immediate session satisfaction

explanation.text: The Logic: Financial-literacy literature (OECD, RBI) confirms that knowledge gained at training decays rapidly. SAS-1300 outcome must be 6-12 month behaviour change, not immediate test scores. Options A, C, D are peripheral. The Trap: Options A, C, D are operational concerns, not the core methodological limitation. Cross-Exam Context: Behavioural-decay logic in OECD Financial Literacy framework and V-A (MF Distributor — investor education). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Schedule a mandatory 9-month follow-up survey in every SAS-1300 engagement letter. Without it, you can only audit training-day learning, not behaviour change.
